summary: iter106 — Court Agreement Alerts + Add-to-Step-4. Backend pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter106_agreement_alerts_and_step4.py: 10/10 PASS. (1) First POST /compare/agree (parent3) triggers an immediate send to parent4 — court_agreement_alerts doc gets last_sent_at set and pending is empty within <10s (Resend accepted). (2) PUT /compare/agree/note on the SAME area within the 6h window does NOT change last_sent_at and leaves exactly 1 pending entry {area:'Pick-Up, Drop-Off & Transitions', kind:'note', note:'Handoffs at 3:15.'}. (3) Second note on the same area REPLACES the pending note entry (de-dupe via $pull then $push); only 1 note remains. (4) Undo (agreed:false) does NOT queue anything (pending list unchanged). (5) After backdating last_sent_at to 7h ago, POST /api/cron/self-assessment-reminders with correct Bearer returns 200 immediately and within <10s pending=[] and last_sent_at updated (backend log 'agreement alerts flushed ... sent=1' visible). (6) Cron without auth or wrong secret -> 401. (7) If parent4 stops sharing while items are pending AND window has expired, flush_one clears pending without sending (verified via direct import of court_agreement_alerts.flush_one). (8) parent1 is safety-flagged, parent1/parent2 never reach ready, so parent1 never gets a court_agreement_alerts doc. (9) email_service.send_agreement_update_alert produces lines '<area>: marked as agreed' and '<area>: a note was added - "<note>"', includes the intent notice in both text and html, and HTML-escapes raw '<ok>' + ampersands (verified via monkeypatched _send). (10) POST /foundation-builder/pdf with fields.co_values containing '(agreed): ' produces a PDF whose text contains 'evidenced their intent' and 'binding agreement'; absent when co_values has no '(agreed): ' line. Frontend (parent4 UI @ 390x844, court door): CourtAgreeCard shows '2 of 6 areas agreed'; opening the Difference popup shows court-agree-all-to-step4 'Add all agreements to Step 4 (2)' and 2 per-row court-agree-to-step4-{i} buttons (only on rows WITH a note — the component uses `{row.note && ...}`). Clicking the first per-row button turns it into 'In Step 4' (disabled), the add-all counter drops to '(1)', and the toast 'Added 1 agreement to Step 4' with description "In 'Agreed co-parenting principles & values'." and action 'Open Step 4' is shown. Clicking add-all adds the remaining one; button becomes 'All agreements are in Step 4' (disabled). GET /foundation-builder/me after flow returns co_values with exactly 2 '<area> (agreed): <note>' lines, no duplicates. No horizontal overflow at 390 (scrollWidth-clientWidth = 0). court-hints-toggle toggles 'Hide Action Buttons' <-> 'Show Action Buttons' correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: court_agreement_alerts.queue_alert uses two sequential update_one calls (one $pull of same-area entries, then $push the new entry). This is correct for de-duping, but between the two writes a concurrent flush_one could observe the queue mid-mutation and send an incomplete bundle. Low likelihood (same user actor), but a single update pipeline with $concatArrays(filter(current, area/kind match), [new]) would make it atomic.

court_agreement_alerts.flush_one clears pending WITHOUT sending when the pair is no longer ready (other=None or court_key mismatch), but ONLY after the 6h window has passed; while the window is still open and the pair breaks, pending items hang around until the next window elapses or the daily cron sweep forces a flush. The cron sweep covers this, so it's fine, but worth noting in docstring.

CourtOrderedView.step4.has uses String.includes(lineOf(r)) against fb.fields.co_values — if a user manually types the exact '<area> (agreed): <note>' line into Step 4 and then clicks Add to Step 4, the button correctly shows 'In Step 4' without a server call. Good. Edge case: if the user edits the note AFTER adding (so lineOf no longer matches), the button will become clickable again and append a second line with the same area but different note. Consider matching on '<area> (agreed):' prefix only to avoid same-area duplication after an edit.

Foundation PDF prints INTENT_NOTICE immediately after any textarea whose value contains ' (agreed): '. Today this is only co_values, but the check is textarea-agnostic — if a future field ever includes '(agreed): ' in free text the notice would also appear under it. Harmless, but worth making 'co_values-only' explicit if that's the intent.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable backend test file: /app/backend/tests/test_iter106_agreement_alerts_and_step4.py (10 cases). Approach notes: (a) the 6h window check in flush_one short-circuits BEFORE the pair-ready check, so to prove 'stop sharing clears pending' you must backdate last_sent_at to >6h before calling flush. (b) The cron 'self-assessment-reminders' endpoint runs flush_all in a background task, so the flush effects appear a short delay after the 200 return. (c) The frontend Difference popup opens via click on court-agree-card; on 390 width an Emergent AI Assistant chat panel can intercept — using page.evaluate(... .click()) via the data-testid works reliably. (d) Per-row 'Add to Step 4' button is only rendered when the row has a note; rows without a note correctly show no button. (e) Resend accepts @test.com addresses in preview — last_sent_at only updates when Resend accepts, which it does here.
rca of the issue: No bugs. The two test failures during authoring were test-calibration (not product bugs): initially I backdated last_sent_at BEFORE queuing the note, which caused immediate send and empty pending; and in the stop-sharing test I forgot that flush_one short-circuits on the window check before reaching the pair-ready clear path. Both tests now set up the state in the correct order.
